sources.name: results.json (the simulation's result file; the luneburg block)

charts.title: What was simulated, and what was not.
charts.takeaway: At a radius of 50 wavelengths, 30 equal shells keep 0.93 of the continuous lens's focal peak and 50 keep 0.99. Everything is a two-dimensional scalar simulation.
charts.n: 9 shell counts and 5 index floors at a radius of 50 wavelengths; no sphere and no hardware

steps.label: A layered cylinder in two dimensions
steps.detail: A scalar wave solution for a plane wave on a cylinder of constant-index shells. No sphere, no absorption and no measurement.

steps.label: Known answer: an empty cylinder
steps.detail: With every shell at index 1 the field should be the plane wave itself. The solver's largest deviation is 2.6 percent in amplitude.

steps.label: Focal peak against the ideal lens
steps.detail: The peak intensity on the rear surface, as a share of the peak of the continuous Luneburg profile, and the width of that peak.

steps.label: 0.93 at 30 shells, 0.99 at 50
steps.detail: Clipping the profile at a minimum index of 1.3 keeps 0.035 of the peak; the refit run shows that loss belongs to the clipping.

charts.title: Focal peak kept by a stepped lens, by number of shells.
charts.takeaway: The focus is lost by degrees: 0.54 of the peak at 10 shells, 0.93 at 30 and 0.99 at 50, where each shell is one wavelength thick.
charts.units: focal peak intensity as a share of the continuous Luneburg lens's peak (1 is the ideal lens)
charts.n: 9 shell counts at a radius of 50 wavelengths, one run each
charts.no_interval: A deterministic solver with one run per shell count. Its own error is about 2.6 percent in amplitude, so shares closer than about 0.05 should not be ranked.
charts.threshold: No bar was set in advance

axis.label: share of the ideal focal peak

charts.title: A raised rim index: the profile clipped, and the profile refitted.
charts.takeaway: At a rim index of 1.3 the clipped profile keeps 0.035 of the peak and a refitted quadratic profile keeps 0.41, so the loss came from clipping and not from the rim index alone.
charts.units: focal peak intensity as a share of the continuous Luneburg lens's peak (1 is the ideal lens)
charts.n: 5 rim indices at a radius of 50 wavelengths, one run each
charts.no_interval: A deterministic solver with one run per rim index; shares closer than about 0.05 should not be ranked.
charts.baseline: The continuous Luneburg profile with a rim index of 1, share 1
charts.threshold: No bar was set in advance; the refit was added after the clipped result was seen

axis.label: share of the ideal focal peak
